source_identity.identity_basis: The sealed checkpoint names a source-bound machine-readable contract; that companion contract at blob 299e3c654affbdd22d6a0fcefacbcf42fa436969 contains this exact finding id. No fuzzy/title join was used.

claim_under_audit: Harn std/external_action uses checkpoint_stage_keyed around remote dispatch, but checkpoint_stage_keyed persists only after the callback returns. Therefore a hard process death after provider acceptance but before adapter return/checkpoint persistence can leave no local completed checkpoint; recovery can invoke dispatch again. Returned/thrown/malformed outcomes are handled more safely, but the inspected local runtime does not itself prove hard-kill exactly-once external effects.

observations: checkpoint_stage_keyed checks for a completed keyed record; when absent it executes f(), then saves the returned value. There is no pre-callback durable in-progress marker in this helper.
external_action_execute calls checkpoint_stage_keyed and performs adapter.dispatch inside the callback before that keyed checkpoint can be saved.

The dispatch request carries intent.idempotency_key, but the ExternalActionAdapter type only requires a dispatch function returning a typed result; the inspected contract does not prove that every adapter/provider enforces provider-side deduplication for that key.

The conformance test strongly verifies same-process replay, terminal denial replay, explicit linked retry, rejected and indeterminate outcomes, and reconciliation. It does not exercise a process SIGKILL at the remote-accept/local-uncommitted seam.
Repository and issue searches found no source-matched SIGKILL external_action test at this seam.

independent_structural_reproduction.method: Deterministic state-machine counterexample derived directly from the pinned checkpoint and external_action source; no worker code or result was reused.
trace: S0: keyed checkpoint for the action fingerprint is absent.
external_action_execute enters checkpoint_stage_keyed; cached record is absent, so callback f starts.
adapter.dispatch is invoked with the stable idempotency_key and the provider accepts/creates the remote effect.
Process is hard-killed before adapter.dispatch returns to Harn, before f returns, and therefore before __checkpoint_stage_keyed_save executes.
After restart, the local keyed checkpoint is still absent. With the same intent/grant, checkpoint_stage_keyed again enters f and invokes adapter.dispatch again.

deduction.returned_or_thrown_adapter_outcome_scope: Once control returns to the runtime, Harn can materialize a terminal or reconciliation-required receipt and same-process/restart replay after that completed checkpoint is substantially better covered. The counterexample is specifically the provider-accepted-before-local-persistence interval.

independent_replication.classification: Structural failure reproduced from official source, but no live provider/process-kill experiment was run in this audit.

scope_corrections: Do not state that Harn necessarily duplicates the remote provider effect. The runtime can re-dispatch locally; whether that becomes a duplicate remote effect depends on provider/adapter idempotency semantics for the supplied stable key.
Do not generalize the gap to ordinary returned exceptions, malformed responses, explicit indeterminate outcomes, or same-process replay; those paths have dedicated receipt/reconciliation tests.
Do not treat comments saying 'at most once' or generic checkpoint 'survive crashes' wording as proof for this particular external side-effect seam, because the save is post-callback.

The finding remains applicable to current public main observed in this audit because the two commits after the worker-pinned revision changed only macOS sandbox/toolchain files and the external_action runtime blob is unchanged.
reopen_conditions: A public Harn hard-kill/fault-injection test exercises provider acceptance followed by process death before adapter return/checkpoint and demonstrates one provider effect after recovery.
external_action gains a durable pre-dispatch/in-progress journal or equivalent supervisor-owned dispatch receipt whose recovery semantics are source-matched and tested.
A concrete provider adapter documents and tests that Harn's stable idempotency_key is mapped to a provider-enforced idempotency primitive across process death.
The external_action runtime/checkpoint blobs change in a way that closes or materially alters this seam.
